[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: 'pick M random items' is read as M independent random picks, so repeats seem acceptable. Rule: in sampling without replacement each member of the set appears at most once, like lottery balls not put back.
[1] misconception (M) -> SampleMayRepeat: wrong rule: A sample drawn without replacement may contain the same item twice. Right rule: Each member of the set appears at most once in the sample.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> SampleMayRepeat: Points to LT: perm[] is first filled with 0..N-1, then the first M shuffle passes run, then perm[0..M-1] is printed. Inconsistent application: the sample is read before all M exchanges are done, or the identity fill is skipped on a trace. (here mixing in: "A sample drawn without replacement may contain the same item twice")

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: sampling without replacement draws a random sample of M items from N in which no item can be chosen twice.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative (Program 1.4.1): perm[j] = j for all j; for i < M, r = i + (int) (Math.random() * (N-i)) and exchange perm[i] with perm[r]; perm[0..M-1] is the sample.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: read M and N, create perm, fill it with the identity, run M exchange passes left to right, then print perm[0] .. perm[M-1].
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: M distinct integers from 0..N-1 (e.g. java Sample 6 16 prints 9 5 13 1 11 8). If M == N the result is a random permutation; if M > N the program throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: each pass exchanges perm[i] with one element to its right, fixing perm[i] as the next sampled item; perm stays a permutation of 0..N-1.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The sample is the first M passes of the shuffle applied to the identity permutation.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: draw lottery numbers or deal a hand. The permutation can also serve as indices into another array (deck[perm[i]]) to sample it without rearranging it.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> SampleMayRepeat: Conservation: perm remains a permutation of 0..N-1 after every exchange, so no value can appear twice for any M <= N; changing M changes only how many passes run.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: use it when the sample must contain distinct items (lotteries, card hands, survey samples). When repeats are allowed (sampling with replacement), independent random indices are simpler.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The sample size cannot exceed the population size. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: M > N on the command line, so perm[i] is indexed at i = N (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException)
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Each pick must come from the items not yet sampled. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: independent picks (int) (Math.random() * N) without exchanging, which can repeat an item
wrong: A sample drawn without replacement may contain the same item twice. | right: Each member of the set appears at most once in the sample.
Sampling without replacement first creates an array of all candidates (perm), then picks from the part not yet chosen.
Sample uses the basic operation underlying shuffling: for each of the first M positions it exchanges perm[i] with a random element to its right.
